title: compute/v1 sandbox creation
description: POST /v1/sandboxes body and its parts. The spec is what ECS compiled from a space's environment declaration (Cloud AGENT-FRAMEWORK §10.4: toolchains mise.toml / mise.lock, dependencies each language's lockfile, heavy bases an OCI image digest). It carries content, never a reference into a space: the compute layer does not know spaces. README.md: contracts/compute/v1/README.md.

lifespan.description: How long the sandbox outlives its last hold. temporary: removed 30 minutes after its last hold ended (or after creation, when never held). long: removed 6 hours after its last hold ended; a long sandbox never held is its owner's own and kept until DELETE /v1/sandboxes/{id}. A failed sandbox is removed 30 minutes after it failed.

holder.description: Optional first hold, as PUT /v1/sandboxes/{id}/holds/{holder} with the default ttl.

network.description: Optional (2026-11-06, additive, AgentCompute#67): the hosts commands in the sandbox may reach. Absent: every public host (as before). It applies once the sandbox is started (the spec's installs run before it); PATCH /v1/computers/{id}/network changes it later. README "Egress".

holderId.description: Opaque to this layer: whoever holds the sandbox names itself (AgentHost uses the conversation id). This layer never interprets it.

ttlSeconds.description: The hold lapses this long after the request unless renewed (the same PUT again).

spec.description: Every part is optional; an empty spec is the default environment image as it is. The whole request body is at most 8 MiB.

image.description: A heavy base pinned by digest. Absent: AgentCompute's environment image (environment-image/).

ref.description: An OCI reference with its digest (registry/repository@sha256:…). A tag alone is refused.

toolchains.description: Toolchains in mise's format (mise, MIT); installed into content-addressed layers keyed by these files.

miseLock.description: The content of mise.lock, when the declaration pins one.

dependencies.description: Dependency sets, each installed by its manager from its manifest and lockfile into `root`, cached by the files' content.

root.description: Absolute path in the sandbox the set is installed for (its files are written there first).

files.description: The manifest and lockfile the manager needs (package.json + package-lock.json, pyproject.toml + uv.lock, Cargo.toml + Cargo.lock, …).

source.description: Provenance only, never read by this layer: which declaration it was compiled from (e.g. "spc_x:.ar/space.yaml#dev@<changeset>"). Shown in logs and errors.

resources.description: Limits of the sandbox: what it may burst to (the CPU quota, the memory cgroup cap, the disk quota); metered and held at these. `requests` is what its node admits it by (the Kubernetes requests/limits model, AgentCompute#167). Larger than any node can hold: 409 COMPUTE_SANDBOX_TOO_LARGE (not retryable, the largest size named). No room now on the node for its requests: 503 COMPUTE_SANDBOX_CAPACITY (retryable, Retry-After, asked vs free per resource). Never silently shrunk.

requests.description: What admission counts on the node (2026-11-08, additive, AgentCompute#167): typical use, each at most its limit (above it: COMPUTE_REQUEST_INVALID). A field left out is the node's default request (from measured use), never more than the limit. A sleeping sandbox counts only its disk request; a failed one nothing. Answered with the defaults filled in.
